classification.difficultyReason: Identify the equal perpendicular sides and apply Pythagoras’ theorem once.

content.prompt:
The equal sides of a right-angled isosceles triangle are 3 cm in length. What is the length of the hypotenuse?

Use the square-root table on printed page 206 to give an approximation correct to 2 decimal places.

answer.worked:
Let $h$ be the hypotenuse length in centimetres. By Pythagoras’ theorem:
$$\begin{align*}h^2&=3^2+3^2\\h^2&=9+9\\h^2&=18\\h&=\sqrt{18}\\h&\approx4.24\end{align*}$$
The table gives $\sqrt{18}\approx4.24$, so the hypotenuse is approximately $4.24\text{ cm}$, correct to 2 decimal places. Its exact length is $\sqrt{18}\text{ cm}=3\sqrt{2}\text{ cm}$.
